title: Technology and diagnostic reasoning: a qualitative international comparison
summary: Anecdotal evidence suggests that doctors in Germany and the UK approach diagnosis in different ways. While British doctors rely mainly on the patient's history and findings from the physical examination, German doctors use technical investigations earlier, more frequently and rely heavily on their results. Doctors, who have migrated from one country to the other during their career, are in a unique position to report on differences in diagnostic approaches. The will be asked to take part in semi-structured interviews, describe and reflect on their experience. Interviews will be transcribed and analyzed with qualitative methods.

interventions.name: Participants will take part semi-structured interviews covering their clinical experience in German and UK. Interviews will be videorecorded, transcribed and analyzed qualitatively

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
qualified physician, work experience both in Germany and UK
Exclusion criteria:
no exclusion criteria
